answer: Join keys are clustered by first-funder: the protocol publishes cluster size s and every member must lock s units of this epoch's per-head payout, struck at close, bound to that key, unlendable. A singleton locks 1. A farm of ten locks ten each. The eleventh head raises s to 11, so it pays 11 and the prior ten each pay one more — the next identity costs more than the last. An honest head on its own island pays one unit; a raven that hatches many keys from one nest pays the rising lock. A river of fresh keys does not reset s, because the funding edge is permanent and cannot be pre-aged.
